name: set_node_properties
title: set_node_properties
description: Changes properties on a node that already exists. This is how you move, rotate, scale, resize, recolour or configure anything after it has been created — without it, every correction means deleting the node and rebuilding it. Values are coerced the same way create_node_safe coerces them: [64, 32] becomes a Vector2, "#ff8800" becomes a Color, a res:// path becomes a loaded Resource. Exported variables from an attached script are settable too, not just engine properties. Every property is validated before any of them is applied, so a bag with one bad value changes nothing.

node.description: Path of the node to modify, relative to the scene root. "." is the root itself.

properties.description: Property name to new value. Must not be empty.

dry_run.description: Validate and report the current values without changing anything.

unchanged.description: Properties that already held the requested value, or whose setter overrode it. Values are read back after writing rather than assumed.

previous.description: The values before the call, so you can undo it yourself.

errors.no_open_scene: No scene is open in the editor.
errors.node_not_editable: The node belongs to an instanced sub-scene.
errors.invalid_properties: One or more values were rejected; nothing was changed. 'details.errors' names each one, with did_you_mean for typos.
